architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added WorkerHeartbeatInterval configuration option to ClientOptions with validation (1-60 seconds) and default of 60s. This allows users to control heartbeat frequency or disable it with negative values.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Heartbeats need to be configurable to balance between resource reporting freshness and network overhead. The 1-60 second range ensures reasonable limits while allowing fine-grained control. Default of 60s provides a conservative starting point.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created new sysinfo package by refactoring existing resourcetuner package, adding gopsutil-based system monitoring with cgroup support for containerized environments.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Reusing existing cgroup infrastructure minimized new code while extending it for broader system monitoring. The sysinfo package provides a clean abstraction for CPU/memory metrics that works across platforms (Linux with cgroups, others with gopsutil).

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented rate limiting for system info collection (100ms minimum refresh interval) using atomic operations and double-checked locking to avoid excessive system calls.
architecture_decisions.rationale: System monitoring calls (especially gopsutil) can be expensive. Rate limiting prevents performance degradation while still providing timely metrics for heartbeats. Atomic operations ensure thread safety with minimal locking overhead.
alternatives_considered: Adaptive intervals based on heartbeat frequency

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Graceful degradation when cgroup stats are unavailable - falls back to system-wide metrics and logs warnings instead of failing.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Workers need to function in diverse environments (containers, VMs, bare metal). The system must work even when cgroups aren't available. Warnings provide visibility without breaking functionality.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extended poller infrastructure to track poll times and integrate with heartbeat metrics collection via pollTimeTracker and heartbeatMetricsHandler.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Polling activity is a key indicator of worker health and load. Integrating poll tracking into existing poller architecture ensures minimal disruption while capturing relevant metrics for heartbeats.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Enhanced worker shutdown to include ShutdownWorker RPC with heartbeat data and proper cleanup of heartbeat registration.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Graceful shutdown allows the server to immediately reallocate tasks instead of waiting for timeouts. Including final heartbeat provides complete lifecycle tracking.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive tests for sysinfo package including rate limiting behavior and metric bounds validation.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Resource monitoring is platform-sensitive and needs robust testing. Rate limiting tests ensure the performance optimization works correctly. Bounds validation ensures metrics stay within expected ranges.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated dynamic configuration and build scripts to enable worker heartbeat features on the server side.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Server-side features need to be enabled for heartbeats to work. Dynamic configuration ensures the feature can be rolled out gradually. Build script updates ensure integration tests run with the feature enabled.

implementation_summary:
The implementation introduces resource-aware worker heartbeating by extending the existing Temporal Go SDK architecture with several key components. First, the existing resourcetuner package was refactored into a new sysinfo package that provides cross-platform CPU and memory monitoring, with special support for cgroups in Linux containers. This package uses gopsutil for system-wide metrics and falls back gracefully when container-specific metrics are unavailable.

The client configuration was extended with a WorkerHeartbeatInterval option, allowing users to control heartbeat frequency between 1-60 seconds or disable it entirely. This integrates with the existing client initialization flow, creating a heartbeat manager when enabled. The poller infrastructure was enhanced to track polling activity through a pollTimeTracker, which feeds into heartbeat metrics about worker activity and load.

Worker lifecycle management was improved to include heartbeat registration on startup and graceful shutdown notification via the ShutdownWorker RPC. The heartbeat callback collects comprehensive metrics including resource utilization, polling statistics, slot supplier information, and plugin metadata. This data is structured into protobuf messages that align with Temporal's API definitions.

The implementation follows Temporal's existing patterns for extensibility, using interfaces like SysInfoProvider to allow different monitoring implementations. It maintains backward compatibility by making heartbeats opt-in via configuration and gracefully degrading when features aren't available. The changes are integrated with the SDK's existing metrics, logging, and interceptor systems, ensuring observability of the new functionality.
